races.title: State House, District 21
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Ya Liu
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina House for District 21 (western Wake County) since 2023. Previously on the Cary Town Council (2019–2023). Holds doctoral degrees in sociology and law, has been a Duke Law faculty member, and has owned a small business. Lives in Cary.

controversies.text: In June 2021 the State Bar's hearing panel suspended Liu's law license for two years, with the suspension stayed for three years under conditions. An audit found she over-disbursed client trust funds and intentionally left her earned fees in the trust account. She says the errors came from inexperience and that she fully complied, so the suspension never took effect.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations on Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Ya Liu was raised, or the year she moved to North Carolina. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing, and no bills or actions of hers that we could confirm on those topics. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year. The source for the State Bar trust-account matter is a short Wikipedia summary with no dates for the suspension, no official documents and no response from Liu. We could not read details of her Duke Law faculty role or her small business.

cands.name: Bryson Johnson
cands.bio: Cybersecurity engineer and small business owner in North Carolina House District 21. Says he has run his business for more than 20 years and held a Top Secret clearance as a contractor supporting U.S. Special Operations. Studied at Campbell University. Has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no record of any elected office or legislative work. His business and security-clearance history comes only from his own survey answers, with no independent confirmation. We found no stated positions or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B visas, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and vouchers. We found no endorsements, news coverage or controversies about him.
